thread:
Jamal: Heads-up — trying to onboard hf/olive-dialogue-v2 and the HF->Redwood conversion is failing because the repo requires trust_remote_code=true. from_pretrained errors with auto_map: 'module object has no attribute OliveConfig'. Tokenizer is a custom python class (olive_tokenizer.py) and special tokens are embedded oddly in config.json. Anyone run into this?

Alex: Yep. Seen variations of that before. Two approaches: 1) load with trust_remote_code and vendor the instantiated tokenizer into a sanitized repo, or 2) patch config.json to remove auto_map and replace with model_type + standard tokenizer_class. For quick testing try: `pip install git+https://github.com/hf/transformers@main` then `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/olive-dialogue-v2', trust_remote_code=True).save_pretrained('./tmp_tok')"`

Mariam: fwiw i'm uncomfortable shipping trust_remote_code for Private deployments. Prefer we vendor tokenizer code into our model bundle and rewrite config.json to remove remote class refs. That means adding `"tokenizer_class": "PreTrainedTokenizerFast"` and providing merges/vocab or tokenizer.json.

Jamal: I tried vendorizing the tokenizer files and ran our converter without trust_remote_code. Conversion completed, but when I tested int8 quantized model we get a chat template formatting regression — system role tokens leak into output and responses truncate mid-turn. Snippet from eval log: ```[INFO] prompt_tokens: [101, 102, ...] generated: "<|system|>You are a helpful assistant..." -> final: "<|system|>You are"```

Sophia: That screams special-token ID remapping during quantization. When tokenizer is vendored, confirm `special_tokens_map` IDs match the actual tokenizer vocabulary after conversion. Run `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<|system|>','<|user|>','<|assistant|>'])` before and after quant step.

Alex: Also check the model forward signature — some of these trust_remote_code models implement custom attention/positional handling. Our inference runtime assumes standard `past_key_values` shapes and `use_cache=True`. If the custom class overrides forward() with different kv ordering or extra return tuples, quant kernels could misalign. You might need a tiny shim that wraps the custom forward into the expected signature.

Mariam: Agreed. For security+reliability i'm opening an infra ticket to support a config-only onboarding path where we accept vendored tokenizer + sanitized config.json but refuse arbitrary Python execution. Ticket ML-1427. Proposed flow: (1) load remote repo locally with trust_remote_code in isolated env, (2) instantiate objects, (3) export canonical tokenizer files + sanitized config.json + model state_dict, (4) delete the isolated env. This avoids executing code at runtime in production.

Jamal: Here's the exact command I used to convert: `python convert_to_redwood.py --hf hf/olive-dialogue-v2 --out ./out --trust-remote False --vendored-tokenizer ./tokfiles` It produced the bundle but chatfmt still broken under int8. I also attached a short eval harness run.

Sophia: Run this quick check before quant: `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('./out'); print(t.convert_tokens_to_ids(['<|system|>','<|user|>','<|assistant|>']))"` If ids differ from the pre-vendored set, something mutated during conversion. Also run sample generations with float32 model to see if the issue is strictly quant-related.

Alex: Operational notes: don't do in-place quantization until tokenization invariants are verified. Use a float->simulated-int8 pass to compare logits/token alignments. If custom attention exists, add a compatibility layer that maps their cached kv format to our runtime's expected layout.

Jamal: Uploading the regression artifacts now to gdrive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A_ml-models/olive-v2/regressions.zip. It includes token diffs and sample prompts. cc @Mariam @Alex.

Mariam: Thanks. I'll review ML-1427 and the artifacts. If anyone has a quick script to sanitize auto_map entries in config.json, paste it here. Otherwise i'll spin one up tonight.

Alex: I can take the token diffs tomorrow morning. Quick tip: when you patch config.json, ensure `architectures` and `model_type` are set to a standard HF value (e.g., "GPT2LMHeadModel" vs a custom OliveXXX class) so our loader picks standard graph kernels. Good catch on the chatfmt regression. :coffee:
